name: How do you make a floor plan feel larger without adding square footage?

mainEntity.name: What design strategies make a custom floor plan feel bigger on the same footprint?
mainEntity.text: What design strategies make a custom floor plan feel bigger on the same footprint?

acceptedAnswer.text: A custom floor plan can feel much larger without increasing the footprint if the layout is efficient and visually open. The biggest gains usually come from reducing wasted circulation, combining related spaces, and creating clear sightlines from one area of the home to another. Open-plan living, better window placement, and smart storage can make a modest footprint feel more generous. Designers also use ceiling height, furniture placement, and connections to outdoor areas to increase the sense of space. A home that borrows light and views from the outside often feels bigger than one with the same square footage but smaller openings. In Los Angeles homes, this is especially valuable because lot sizes can be tight and buildable area may be limited. The goal is not just to add space visually, but to make every square foot work harder.
acceptedAnswer.description: A plan can feel larger by reducing hallways, opening shared spaces, improving sightlines, using larger windows, and placing storage efficiently. Good circulation and daylight often matter more than raw square footage when a home needs to feel spacious.
